 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. The NFL is a land of opportunity for young players to prove they're build for the pros. 
 Cleveland Browns rookie Emmanuel McNeil-Warren is going to get a major opportunity on Sunday when the Houston Texans visit Huntington Bank Field. 
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement With the team ruling out veteran safety Ronnie Hickman due to a concussion, McNeil-Warren, better known as E-Man among his teammates, will take his place as Cleveland's starting free safety. It won't be the first time the second-round pick has started a game, but it's the first time he'll start at one of the two main safety spots this season.
 "It feels good just to hear your name called, just be ready to step up when one of your teammates down," he said of the opportunity on Thursday . "Go out there, execute, play good, try to get them in for the team."
 The Toledo product has spent the first nine weeks of the season prepping for this moment. He started 2026 primarily as a special-teamer, but has seen his snaps increase week-over-week from 14 in Week 1 to a little over 30 in each of the last two games. 
 Cleveland Browns Turn Back to Deshaun Watson, Jared Verse Takes Accountability as HUGE Matchup Looms Cleveland Browns Turn Back to Deshaun Watson, Jared Verse Takes Accountability as HUGE Matchup LoomsThe Cleveland Browns are staring down a massive matchup on Sunday that is all but a Playoff Game against the Houston Texans. They turn back to Deshaun Watson... 
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement He played a season-high 54 snaps in Week 6 after fellow safety Grant Delpit exited the team's 13-10 win over Baltimore just a few plays into the game following a hit to the head that landed him in the concussion protocol. 
 Now he'll start next to Delpit, where the communication between the two will be key to slowing down an elite Texans passing attack led by quarterback C.J. Stroud and his deep arsenal of weapons. Ironing out some of those kinks has been a focus for the two at practice this week. 
 "Just taking it day by day. Just having a preparation day by day. Just try to follow [Ronnie's] footsteps with communication," E-man said. "Make sure everybody's straight, everybody on point so the DBs will be all together and play fast together." 
 Delpit can relate to being a young player and having to absorb a lot all at once. 
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "You're going to have to communicate to everybody around you that everybody's relying on you, so that's something I had to learn too as a young player growing up," he said. "The more you communicate, the better everybody around you is going to be." 
 Delpit went on to explain why game day is often the best teacher for a rookie. Fortunately, McNeil-Warren has gained plenty of relevant experience already. 
 "I lean on him very much, just him just being like a vet to me, asking him questions and learning the game more," Eman said of using Delpit as a resource. "So it'll be great to be out there with him." 
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement In that game he filled in for Delpit, the rookie DB finished with six combined tackles, one for a loss and a pass breakup. On the season he has 42 combined tackles, three of them for a loss and three pass breakups. 
 His next goal: snare his first career interception. And he hopes it comes Sunday. 
 "It's coming for sure," he said. "God's plan for real, just praying for it to come my way. So this time, make a game-changing play."
